correctness.rationale: A fresh vertex is specified by a downset L and an upset U with L strictly below U pairwise. These conditions handle every transitivity clause, and the generic poset realizes each profile, with ultrahomogeneity identifying the complete types. If both are nonempty they use only minima for L and maxima for U, with disjoint index sets. If only L can be nonempty, the downset has no maxima, has precisely one maximum and its n−1 mandatory minima, or has all minima and a nonempty subset of maxima. These disjoint cases give the displayed T_n after accounting for the all-incomparable profile. The base group preserves layers, including for n=2, and must preserve the unique missing matched relation, so it permutes the indices simultaneously. In the one-sided exceptional case there is a second orbit of degree n; in the two-sided case the ordered disjoint index sizes determine the orbit. This yields J_n and O_n, with the empty profile counted only once. Each base automorphism extends and equal profiles fixing the base are conjugate by ultrahomogeneity. The term 'orbit-size polynomial' refers to the two type cardinalities, not the cardinality of an orbit; the displayed definition is unambiguous. An independently written bit-row transitivity test and paired-state orbit classification compared every coefficient for n=2 through 6: label counts 19,47,119,315,867 and orbit counts 12,18,25,33,42. Replay: python3 -B /workspace/repro/2.py; output /workspace/repro/2.log. This is finite corroboration, not the general proof.
